brief: On the year's lowest-volume session (12 Oct 2026, exchange volumes -20.7% vs the 20-day average), the S&P closed -6bps at 7,807 with a $3bn buy imbalance at the close. Nasdaq fell 71bps, Russell 2000 fell 41bps, and Dow rose 38bps. Semiconductors underperformed, led lower by Memory, which the desk attributes to China's progress in memory chip production, follow-through weakness from Korea's KOSPI (-365bps), and a continuing shift in flows toward selling memory and HDD names into last week's close. Mag7 traded firm, with Meta up 4% on its "Muse Wonder" launch and an ongoing flight-to-quality rotation into the group. Crude extended gains on weekend escalation in the Middle East. Overall floor activity was rated a 2 of 10, with client skews described as benign. The vol desk was quiet with fixed income closed for the holiday. The S&P's one-week implied move through Friday printed at 1% (about 96bps), among the lowest in roughly six years. Clients bought downside put spreads in HYG given the bond market closure. Citing a lack of conviction, low sentiment, and narrow breadth, the desk said S&P upside looks cheap into month-end and prefers owning 30 October SPY/QQQ gamma for earnings exposure without midterm-election premium.
